newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Finance Minister says rates too high.
newsitem.headline: Israel Finance Minister says rates too high.

text.p: Israel Finance Minister Dan Meridor said interest rates should be lower and this was something the government was working on.

"I am not among those who bless every day the level of interest rates, to put it mildly," Meridor said in remarks broadcast on Israel Radio. "I think all in all it is desirable that interest rates should be lower. This is a process that we are talking about and working on."
Meridor said that because interest rates were so high, few people were taking out mortgages.
He declined to expand further on the matter, saying it would not be "productive" to discuss it in public.

In a little more than a month the independent Bank of Israel has lowered interest rates twice -- by 0.7 percentage point in late July and by 0.5 percentage point last week -- bringing its key lending rate to an annualised 15.8 percent.
But the cuts were not enough to appease critics, especially business leaders who warn of a slowdown in the economy.
Critics also blame the present interest rate level for an overvalued shekel and weak stock prices.
The Bank of Israel says it must maintain a tight monetary policy to control inflation, especially in light of the government's widening budget deficit.
